method: Components are catalog tools that implement a surface from changes.json directly: ledger codecs, node-to-client clients, chain indexers and query services, nodes, script toolchains, transaction builders, hardware signing and devnet tooling.

Each repository was cloned at its default-branch head (observed.revision) and searched case-insensitively for Dijkstra; GitHub issues and pull requests mentioning Dijkstra were retrieved the same day.
Node-to-client readiness is whether the client offers V23 (wire value 32791), the only version node 11.2.1 accepts (ouroboros-consensus 5.4.0.0).

Codec readiness is compared with the target ledger CDDL (cardano-ledger 95b36905, whose CDDL is identical to 54e24ba4's) after removing comments and whitespace; Haskell consumers are compared through the cardano-ledger-dijkstra version their CHaP index-state or constraints select.
Status is per surface group; a component is only as ready as its worst assessment. no-evidence is never a pass.

firstReleases names, per release line, the earliest tag whose source contains every cited source quote (for gouroboros ledger types: the earliest tag whose vendored Dijkstra CDDL is identical to the one compared with the target; for plutus-ledger-api: the target component-set version). Consumer pins are judged only against firstReleases.

in-progress needs visible work toward the target definitions (a branch, an open pull request, or unreleased code on the default branch). A release built only against superseded Dijkstra definitions, with no such work, is a gap.

R4: a devnet result can back an assessment as evidence of kind devnet, naming the check in devnet.json and the version exercised. verified needs a passing result; a failing result cannot back released or verified. Where the target CDDL and the node disagree, the node at the pinned target revision decides: its Dijkstra header is the ten-field Praos header (devnet check block-shape).

Blockfrost is one component (owner decision, 2026-10-22): its source is the run-your-own backend, which the hosted API runs, so hosted and self-hosted consumers share its statuses. Maestro is deprecated and is not a component; the classification treats a shipped call to it as a gap.

New tagged-node runtime results replace integration-run observations only after execution; the complete previous registers are archived in dijkstra-history/2026-10-26-integration.

assessments.summary: The language enum stops at PlutusV3, so cost models and witnesses for PlutusV4 (language 3) cannot be represented or decoded.

The transaction body decoder handles keys up to 22 and rejects any other key, so bodies with sub-transactions, account keys (23-27) fail to decode; guards on key 14 fail as required signers. On the 11.2.1 devnet 17.0.0, 15.0.3 and 18.0.0-beta.1 decode plain Dijkstra transactions but re-encode them in the legacy four-element form, and fail on every direct deposit, sub-transaction, guard, balance interval and PlutusV4 reference script.

Blocks are decoded in the segregated form (header, transaction bodies, witness sets, auxiliary data, invalid transactions); Dijkstra's [header, block_body] does not match. On the 11.2.1 devnet 17.0.0, 15.0.3 and 18.0.0-beta.1 decode none of 336 Dijkstra blocks.
Protocol parameter updates decode keys up to 33 and reject any other key, so updates of the Dijkstra parameters (34-56) fail.
A pool registration certificate must have exactly ten elements; one carrying Dijkstra's optional BLS key is rejected.

No Dijkstra reference at the observed revision (case-insensitive search of tracked files, lockfiles excluded) and no issue or pull request mentioning Dijkstra. CSL has no era tag of its own, and its builder does not model the Dijkstra rules.

The transaction body ends at key 22 (donation); Dijkstra adds body keys 23-27 (sub-transactions, required guards, direct deposits, balance intervals) and redefines key 14 as guards, so CML cannot decode transactions that use them. On the devnet it rejects every three-element Dijkstra transaction, even plain payments (cml-decoding).
Languages stop at PlutusV3 (language 2); PlutusV4 is language 3 with script tag 4 and witness key 8.
Protocol parameter updates stop at key 33; Dijkstra adds keys 34-56.
pool_params ends at pool_metadata, without Dijkstra's optional BLS key.

assessments.summary: 0.8.0-pre8 (prerelease, 2026-11-15) ships PR #748's era-aware reader and Dijkstra models (keys 23-27, guards on key 14). Built with them and written with serialize(Era.Dijkstra), a payment, direct deposits, a key guard, a balance interval, a PlutusV4 reference script, lock and spend, and a sub-transaction were all accepted on the devnet, including when signed through the Transaction object (devnet check ccl-dijkstra-transactions). Read with Era.Dijkstra, 31 of the 32 devnet encodings give the on-chain id; the PlutusV4 guard transaction does not, because the model re-encodes its body keys in another order than cardano-cli wrote them (RawTx gives the right id).
